content:
Last month we ran a poll, and the overwhelming majority of 9to5Mac readers agreed that Apple should abandon its advertising business.

Advertising has now landed on Apple Maps in the United States and Canada, and I find it, as expected, rather distasteful…

Apple first warned everyone back in March that ads would start appearing in the Maps app at some point over the summer. We spotted these ads for the first time yesterday, and Apple has confirmed that the rollout has been underway for the past few days. All users in the U.S. and Canada will see them within the next few weeks.

  • Before search: "Suggested places" within the search page will display ads.
  • After search: ads will appear within search results in suitable locations.

Apple says that privacy is a major concern.

I believe all of the above to be entirely true, but I still find the move extremely poor in taste for two reasons.

First, while Apple is not using any tracking to deliver personalised ads, almost every other app and website does. Most people will assume that the iPhone maker does too — even if that perception is unfair — and it damages the company's long-standing image as a guardian of user privacy.

Second, it looks cheap. Ads are an unavoidable 'necessary evil' in the app and website ecosystem: it's because of them that free apps and websites can keep the lights on. But Apple doesn't need ad revenue to keep going: its hardware already sells at a premium. Ads simply don't fit the company's brand image.

I believe it was John Gruber who compared advertising in Apple apps to those awful Intel Inside stickers on cheap Windows laptops. We all understand that makers of cheap laptops need to squeeze every possible revenue stream, but we'd never have expected Apple to slap such stickers on a MacBook to cheapen the brand. So why should we accept ads in the built-in apps on Apple devices?

I still maintain that Apple has absolutely no need to plant a flag in the advertising business.
